newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee ends steady at 35.89, RBI defends dlr.
newsitem.headline: India rupee ends steady at 35.89, RBI defends dlr.

text.p: The Indian rupee closed at 35.890/8950 against the dollar on Wednesday, little changed from the opening 35.89/90, dealers said.
"There was mild (dollar) demand in the morning, with the rupee touching a low of 35.8975," said a bank dealer.
The exchange rate soon stabilised at 35.8850/8900, he said.
The day's range was between 35.8850 and 35.8975 rupees.

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was active in the spot market buying dollars in small amounts at 35.8950 rupees, dealers said. Dollar supply rose in the afternoon session because of inflows from markets outside Bombay, they said.
A leading Calcutta-based state-run bank did not buy aggressively but picked up dollars from banks approaching it, dealers said.
Forward dollar premia fell by as much as three to four paise on corporate selling, dealers said.
The six month annualised premium closed at 6.80 percent on Wednesday, down from the previous close of 7.03 percent.
"Talk of interest rate cut also influenced the market," said a dealer, referring to recent statements from the finance minister and the RBI on the need to reduce interest rates.
